our_argument_summary: Standard Sq theory (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017; Kim & Chang 2018) predicts the −10.9 nT BOU 2017 eclipse signal without dome geometry. The dome derives FSF = H(r)/r from V12 (Pearson r ≈ 0.9999), but the absolute magnitude at the BOU anchor is imported from the 2017 observation itself and reused as the 2026 baseline. The verdict text now pre-registers an α∈{0.8,1.0,1.2} coverage-exponent sensitivity check, a ≤30%-of-in-band-median ceiling for >50° CGM stations, and a smooth-f(mag_lat) upgrade path — meant to convert the 2026 European eclipse into a clean prospective discrimination between FSF and Sq-magnetic-latitude scaling. Plus Kp asymmetry, post-hoc framing, and a cross-reference to Section 1.8 (coordinate collapse).

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py hardcodes BOU target = -10.9 nT and baseline = -10.9 nT (identical). FSF table per station is computed from r·tan(θ)=8537·exp(-r/8619) and published as a 9-row constant. Eclipse 'check' = predicted vs. observed comparison with the predicted side pre-anchored to the observation.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Anchor magnitude: hardcoded. Per-station FSF: computed from V12 (verifiable). Live 2026 observation: will be fetched, but the prediction it is checked against has the 2017 number baked in.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: monitor.py imposes Kp<2 quiet-day filter for 2026 validation; 2017 baseline was recorded at Kp≈3 (unsettled). Asymmetric evidentiary standard.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None new in c11. Prior cycles' code-claim audits stand.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: monitor.py hardcodes both the −10.9 nT target and baseline; FSF scaling is computed but its anchor is a static 2017 observation. The 2026 fetch validates the predicted value, but the predicted value has the same number baked in as the observation.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Eclipse-induced magnetic perturbations are Sq-suppression — the canonical Chapman/Yamazaki & Maute account. Dome reuses identical physical mechanism (ionospheric conductivity drop from shadow-occluded UV) and rebrands it as confirmation of dome geometry.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: 2017 BOU observation is in the public INTERMAGNET archive and predates the dome's WIN claim. monitor.py's data-fetch line and the hardcoded target appear in the same commit, so the prediction-then-data ordering required by the dome author's own definition cannot be checked from git history.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: FSF = H(r)/r genuinely follows from V12 (Pearson 0.9999, reproduced in c8 and unchanged). But this is a station-to-station ratio. The absolute magnitude at the BOU anchor is imported from the 2017 observation, not derived from any dome parameter — the inter-station scaling can be right while the magnitude is still observation-anchored.

holes_found.description: Standard-model competing prediction misclassifies at least HAD and ESK (and likely NGK) as 'in-band' when they are >50° CGM. The new verdict text says 'most stations sit inside the 30°–50° CGM band... only LER (≳58° CGM) clearly outside' but a centered-dipole calculation (epoch 2020, pole 80.65°N/287.32°E) places HAD at ≈53.6° CGM, ESK at ≈57.5° CGM, NGK at ≈51.9° CGM, and LER at ≈61.8° CGM. CGM differs from centered-dipole by a few degrees at these latitudes but not enough to move 53-57° back below 50°. So 3 of 9 stations (HAD, ESK, LER) — not 1 — are clearly outside the 30-50° band, with NGK marginal. The 'binary classifier' competing prediction this WIN has committed to therefore predicts ≤30% of in-band median (i.e., ≤≈-3 nT) for HAD/ESK/LER rather than the in-band value the text implies. The dome's prediction for HAD is -12.8 nT (one of its strongest); for ESK -10.3; for LER -9.5. The standard-model side of the 2026 test, as currently described, would over-predict in-band amplitude for two stations and weaken the discriminatory contrast that the new pre-registration was meant to establish.
holes_found.recommendation: Recompute CGM latitudes for all 9 stations using the IGRF-14 model (epoch 2026) and the IAGA observatory registry. Restate which stations are in-band vs. out-of-band BEFORE the eclipse occurs (the pre-registration only holds if the band-membership is fixed pre-data-arrival). Edit the verdict text to replace 'only LER (≳58° CGM) clearly outside' with the corrected count (likely 'HAD, ESK, and LER are outside the 30-50° CGM band; NGK sits near the upper edge'). This actually strengthens the discrimination — three stations with predicted suppression vs. six in-band lets us distinguish FSF (smooth geographic) from Sq (binary-by-magnetic-latitude) more clearly than the current 1-out-of-9 framing.

holes_found.description: The ≤30%-of-in-band-median ceiling for >50° CGM stations is self-disclosed as 'first-order, citation-honest pre-registration' but the underlying paper (Kim & Chang 2018) does not tabulate the attenuation magnitude — only that there IS a Z-component decrease outside the band. The text says 'we therefore fix the upper bound at 30%... as a first-order, citation-honest pre-registration. If the 39-eclipse binned amplitudes become accessible we will replace this bound with a paper-derived amplitude.' Hole [1] above identifies HAD, ESK, LER (and possibly NGK) as out-of-band, so this 30% parameter now governs the standard-model prediction for 3-4 of the 9 stations — not 1. A dome defender will argue the competing prediction is materially dependent on a parameter the review admits is not paper-derived. The 'citation-honest' framing is candid but doesn't paper over the substantive issue that the discrimination machinery has a free parameter on the standard-model side too.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) attempt one more pass at Kim & Chang's binned-amplitude supplementary data (the 39-eclipse ensemble may have it tabulated somewhere — at minimum cite the figure/table that documents the systematic decrease, even if the magnitude is read off rather than tabulated), or (b) replace the ≤30% upper bound with a symmetric two-sided pre-registered band (e.g., 20-50% of in-band median, centred at ~35%) and pre-register that the test is informative only if observations fall outside that wider band. (b) is more defensible because it makes the standard-model prediction quantitative and explicitly bounded, with the breadth motivated by acknowledged paper-gap rather than picked. Either path closes the 'made-up number' attack vector.

holes_found.description: The α ∈ {0.8, 1.0, 1.2} coverage-exponent sensitivity range is unjustified. The text introduces α as a way to probe nonlinear-coverage effects but does not motivate why 0.8 and 1.2 are the right endpoints. Physical Sq-coverage response can be sublinear (saturation of conductivity drop near totality) or superlinear (cumulative ionization recovery time near sub-totality limb), and published Sq treatments would point at specific exponent ranges from conductivity-integral derivations. A defender will ask 'why ±20%? Why not ±50%?' and the answer in the text is silent.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a one-clause justification: 'the ±20% range brackets the Sq conductivity integral's dependence on coverage at first order [cite reference if available, or note that this is an a priori adopted range for sensitivity-testing rather than a derived bound].' Better yet, run the post-eclipse residual analysis at α = 0.5 and 1.5 as well — if the FSF-vs-mag-lat ranking is stable across α ∈ [0.5, 1.5] the discrimination claim is robust; if it flips inside that wider range the review should say so.

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c6/c7/c8/c9/c10: 'Chapman–Sq ionospheric framework' (em-dash) in `finding` vs. 'Chapman Sq ionospheric framework' (space, no dash) in `detail_evidence` and `detail_verdict_text`. Five cycles flagged, EXP-244 promised cluster-wide canonicalization, the inconsistency remains. WIN-068 still uses the spaced form per c10 hole [0]. A defender will read both spellings on the same WIN page and conclude the cluster has not been canonicalized despite stated intent.
holes_found.recommendation: Pick one — either accept 'Chapman–Sq' as a project-coined term and apply globally (replace `finding` 'Chapman–Sq' → standardize; cascade to WIN-025/068), or revert all instances to 'Sq ionospheric framework (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017)' which is closer to standard literature usage. This is a one-line patch; it should not survive into c12.

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c6/c7/c8/c9/c10: family non-uniqueness still rests on a self-acknowledged 'we have not exhaustively swept alternative parametrizations (Gaussian, power-law, piecewise-linear, etc.) against the nine-station FSF table' disclaimer. The c11 text adds the new clause '... the dome, however, has not demonstrated that the exponential form is uniquely required either' which is honest but does not make the discriminating claim. Six cycles is a long time to leave the same empirical hole open. The fix is bounded — one alternative H(r) function fitted to the BOU + EBR/SPT/COI calibration anchors and evaluated at the 9 stations is a 50-line script.
holes_found.recommendation: Spawn an EXP to produce one worked alternative — Gaussian H(r) = A·exp(-(r/L)^2) and a generalized exponential H(r) = A·exp(-(r/L)^β) are the natural first picks. Fit each to two calibration anchors (BOU + one of EBR/SPT/COI), compute the implied FSF at all 9 stations, and compare to the dome's published FSF values. If the alternatives land within 3% of the dome's FSFs, the family argument is empirically confirmed and the hole closes permanently. If they diverge by >>3%, the dome's exponential is genuinely a tight fit and we should retract the family claim and acknowledge the dome's geometric form is uniquely good at reproducing its own table — which is still NOT a magnitude-derivation argument but is a stronger geometric one than the current text concedes.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's binary use of c (in WIN-029, f = c/4H) and v_a = 1.574c (in WIN-001, f = v_a/(2r_disc)) on the same 'aetheric circuit' should be exploited in WIN-010's verdict text as additional evidence the dome's parameter fitting is operational, not theoretical. The Chapman Sq framework, in contrast, uses ONE conductivity profile and ONE speed of light to predict the eclipse signal, the Schumann band, and the diurnal Sq variation. Argumentative leverage: the dome needs different propagation speeds for different WINs in the same circuit; standard physics needs one set of constants. (Currently this lives only in WIN-001/WIN-002 prose. WIN-010's verdict could add one sentence cross-referencing it.)

stronger_arguments.description: If hole [1]'s corrected CGM-latitude classification is applied (HAD/ESK/LER all >50°), the 9-station test becomes a true 6-vs-3 discrimination: standard model predicts in-band amplitude for 6 stations and suppressed amplitude for 3, while the dome's FSF predicts smooth geographic variation across all 9 with NO break at the geomagnetic-latitude boundary. That break-vs-no-break is a sharp, statistically clean test signature — much stronger than the current 1-out-of-9 framing implies. The corrected text should LEAN INTO this rather than treat it as a defect.

kernel_of_truth.description: The FSF=H(r)/r derivation from V12 is real — the dome's coordinate equation r·tan(θ) = 8537·exp(-r/8619) genuinely reproduces its nine published FSF values to Pearson 0.9999, and the current detail_evidence (WIN-010 wins.json:detail_evidence) acknowledges this with the explicit Pearson and the 0.6%/2.78% match-accuracy figures. The new α-sensitivity check and the smooth-f(mag_lat) upgrade-path additions (see WIN-010 wins.json:detail_verdict_text new clauses on 'coverage-response exponent α ∈ {0.8, 1.0, 1.2}' and 'if the 39-eclipse binned amplitudes become accessible we will instead fit a smooth f(mag_lat)') are genuine methodological improvements; the WIN now pre-registers more falsifiable structure than it did at c10. The dome is honestly publishing per-station predictions in advance of the 2026-08-12 eclipse and the review is honestly committing to a competing prediction in the same window.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Granting the FSF derivation does not save the claim because the BOU −10.9 nT absolute magnitude is still imported from the 2017 observation (see WIN-010 wins.json:detail_evidence 'the absolute magnitude at the Boulder anchor (−10.9 nT) is imported from the 2017 observation and reused as the 2026 baseline'). The new pre-registered sensitivity machinery is methodologically sound but still vulnerable on three operationally-substantive points: (a) hole [1] — the standard-model side misclassifies HAD/ESK as in-band when they are not, weakening the discrimination the pre-registration was meant to establish; (b) hole [2] — the ≤30% ceiling for out-of-band stations is admitted-non-paper-derived and now governs the prediction for 3-4 stations, not 1; (c) hole [5] (carry-over) — the family non-uniqueness claim still rests on a 'we have not swept' disclaimer six cycles after first flagging. A defender accepting the kernel can still attack three specific operational points the review hasn't closed.

deeper_analysis:
The c11 update did real work on the c10 nonlinear-coverage hole — the α∈{0.8,1.0,1.2} sensitivity check is exactly the kind of pre-registered robustness probe the c10 recommendation asked for, and the candid acknowledgement that 'we have not swept alternative H(r) parametrizations' and that the binary classifier yields 'only 2-3 unique predicted values across nine stations' demonstrates good-faith intellectual honesty about open methodological weaknesses. The smooth-f(mag_lat) upgrade path is a sensible contingent improvement.

The substantive new finding (hole [1]) emerged from doing Lens C quantitative verification on the new CGM-band claim. The text's pre-registered competing prediction declares only LER as out-of-band, but a centered-dipole computation places HAD at ≈53.6°, ESK at ≈57.5°, NGK at ≈51.9°, and LER at ≈61.8° — three (and possibly four) of nine stations outside the 30-50° band, not one. This is not a fatal flaw — it's a correctable pre-registration error before the eclipse occurs (2026-08-12 is still 60 days out). But it MUST be corrected before the eclipse, because the standard-model prediction is now operating on an incorrect station classification. The fix actually STRENGTHENS the test: 6-in vs 3-out is a much sharper FSF-vs-Sq discrimination signature than 8-in vs 1-out.

The ≤30% upper bound (hole [2]) is more philosophically interesting. The text candidly admits it is not paper-derived, and frames the admission as 'first-order, citation-honest pre-registration.' That framing is intellectually credible but creates a defensive vulnerability: a fair-minded dome defender can reasonably point out that the standard-model competing prediction has a free parameter on its side too. The right fix is either to ground the 30% in a paper-derived figure (if accessible) or to widen the pre-registered band to two-sided 20-50% and pre-register that the test is informative only if observations fall OUTSIDE that band on either side.

The four carry-over holes (Chapman–Sq vs Chapman Sq spelling, family non-uniqueness, Kim & Chang page range, stylistic redundancy) are all minor and slow-burning. The family non-uniqueness hole is the most worth closing — six cycles of 'we have not swept' is starting to look avoidable. Spawning one EXP to fit one Gaussian and one generalized-exponential H(r) and report the resulting 9-station FSF tables would close the hole permanently in one analyst pass.

No carry-over hole has a matching open issue in monitor/decisions/open-issues.json (search returned 0 hits for WIN-010), so unresolved_prior_cycle is empty here — the decider should be prompted to either create issues for the persisting items or accept them as 'live but not blocking' status. The verdict 'Std Model Explains' continues to hold; recommendation is minor_edit with a substantive (but bounded) CGM-classification fix on the discrimination machinery.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender accepting the review's own methodology can construct this rebuttal: 'Granted that FSF=H(r)/r derives from V12 and the absolute BOU magnitude is anchor-imported. Granted the Kp asymmetry and the post-hoc framing. But the review's new competing prediction is materially weaker than the dome's: (1) the dome publishes 9 distinct FSF values; the standard-model binary classifier yields only 2-3 unique predicted amplitudes — that's a fundamentally less informative prediction. (2) The standard-model side has its own free parameter (the ≤30% out-of-band ceiling) which the review itself admits is not paper-derived. (3) The review concedes it has not produced a single alternative H(r) family member that fits the calibration anchors AND the 9-station FSF table — until it does, the dome's exponential form is the ONLY demonstrated parameterization. (4) The dome's geographic-latitude scaling and the magnetic-latitude scaling may not be cleanly separable when most stations sit in the 30-50° band: at this epoch the geographic-latitude axis correlates strongly with CGM latitude across the European core, so the discrimination claim depends on getting the ~3 out-of-band stations right — but the review's competing prediction misclassifies which stations those are. The 2026 test, on its current pre-registration, doesn't cleanly distinguish FSF from Sq; both predictions are similar across 6-7 of 9 stations, the discriminating stations are LER (clearly outside) and possibly HAD/ESK (depending on how the band-cut is enforced), and the standard-model prediction for those stations rests on the 30% ceiling free parameter. A fair conclusion at this stage: the test is set up to be inconclusive unless observations land in a specific window the review has not bracketed.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: This defense is genuinely strong (4/5) and several of its sub-points are restatements of holes [1], [2], and [5] that the review can preemptively neutralize before the eclipse: (a) Fix the CGM-band classification (hole [1]) to correctly identify HAD/ESK/LER as out-of-band — this turns the 'weak discrimination' attack into a 6-vs-3 discrimination signature. (b) Either ground the 30% ceiling in a paper figure or widen it to a symmetric pre-registered band with explicit informativeness conditions (hole [2]) — this neutralizes the 'standard-model has free parameters too' attack. (c) Spawn one EXP to fit Gaussian and generalized-exponential H(r) alternatives and report the implied 9-station FSF tables (hole [5]) — this either closes the family non-uniqueness claim empirically or honestly retracts it. With these three fixes, the defense collapses to 'the test is still genuinely prospective and falsifiable — let's wait for the data' — which is what the review wants the dome defender to say.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: Two minor cross-WIN issues, both inherited from c10 (not new in c11): (a) Chapman–Sq vs Chapman Sq spelling inconsistency persists across WIN-010/025/068 cluster (see hole [4]); (b) Kim & Chang page range was '2040-2054' in WIN-068 text (c10 flagged it for ISS-1287 TOC check) and is now '2040-2049' in WIN-010 (see hole [6]). Substantive arguments are consistent — all three WINs invoke the same Chapman-Sq mechanism for the same kind of eclipse signal, the cluster note acknowledging shared mechanism is present in the verdict text, and no contradictory factual claims exist between WINs. The bookkeeping inconsistencies should be closed in one cluster pass but don't undermine the cluster's structural integrity.

claims_checked: Centered-dipole CGM latitude for 8 of the 9 stations in the 2026-08-12 eclipse pre-registration (SNK code unresolved). Compared against the text's claim 'most stations sit inside the 30°–50° CGM band... only LER (≳58° CGM) clearly outside.'
quantitative_verification.computations: Used IGRF-14 epoch 2020 centered-dipole pole position (80.65°N, 287.32°E). For each station φ,λ: sin(φ_m) = sin(φ_p)·sin(φ) + cos(φ_p)·cos(φ)·cos(λ-λ_p). Results: COI 43.71°, EBR 42.89°, SPT 42.42°, CLF 49.62°, NGK 51.85°, HAD 53.59°, ESK 57.54°, LER 61.80°. CGM differs from centered-dipole by a few degrees at these latitudes but not enough to move 53-57° stations back below 50°.
quantitative_verification.discrepancies: Text says 'only LER clearly outside' the 30-50° band; computation shows HAD, ESK, and LER are clearly outside, with NGK at the boundary. Three stations (possibly four) belong to the out-of-band suppressed-amplitude cohort under the binary classifier, not one. See hole [1].

summary_for_decider: WIN-010 c11 change-driven review. Verdict (Std Model Explains) HOLDS. New material in detail_verdict_text since c10 includes the α∈{0.8,1.0,1.2} coverage-exponent sensitivity check (good — addresses c10 hole [1]), a ≤30%-of-in-band-median ceiling for >50° CGM stations (now needs strengthening — see hole [2]), and an explicit smooth-f(mag_lat) upgrade path. NEW substantive finding (hole [1], moderate): the standard-model competing prediction misclassifies HAD/ESK as in-band when centered-dipole CGM-latitude calculation places them outside the 30-50° band — text says 'only LER clearly outside' but computation says HAD/ESK/LER all >50°. This is correctable pre-eclipse (2026-08-12 is 60 days out) and the fix actually strengthens the discrimination (6-in vs 3-out is sharper than 8-in vs 1-out). Hole [2] (moderate): the ≤30% out-of-band ceiling is admitted-non-paper-derived and now governs 3-4 stations not 1; recommend either paper-grounding or widening to a two-sided pre-registered band. Four carry-over minors from c10: hyphenation inconsistency (hole [4]), family non-uniqueness 'we haven't swept' disclaimer (hole [5] — six cycles open, worth spawning one EXP to close), Kim & Chang page range unverified (hole [6]), stylistic redundancy (hole [7]). NO open issues currently exist for WIN-010 — recommend the decider either create issues for the persisting carry-over items (hole [5] in particular) or document them as accepted live limitations. Recommended_action: minor_edit. Confidence 0.88. No verdict change.
